a.request: Matching each result to its race by `raceId`, group by race name (`races.name`) and compute each race name's total `points` and average `laps`. Keep race names whose total points are greater than the average of those totals across all race names. Return one row with: the sum of the kept race names' total points; the plain average of their per-race-name average laps, each race name counting equally; and the average amount by which their totals exceed the average total.
a.sql: WITH race_name_totals AS (SELECT r.name, SUM(res.points) AS total_points, AVG(CAST(res.laps AS REAL)) AS avg_laps FROM results AS res JOIN races AS r ON r.raceId = res.raceId GROUP BY r.name), overall AS (SELECT AVG(total_points) AS avg_total FROM race_name_totals) SELECT SUM(t.total_points) AS sum_total_points, AVG(t.avg_laps) AS avg_laps, AVG(t.total_points - o.avg_total) AS avg_excess_points FROM race_name_totals AS t CROSS JOIN overall AS o WHERE t.total_points > o.avg_total

c.request: Looking at race results by race name (`races.name`, matched to results by `raceId`), which race names have a total of `points` above the average total across race names? For those race names together, give me in one row their combined total points, their average laps completed, and the average amount by which their totals exceed the average total. For race names with above-average total points, the laps figure is the plain mean of each race name's average laps.
c.sql: WITH race_name_totals AS (SELECT r.name, SUM(res.points) AS total_points, AVG(CAST(res.laps AS REAL)) AS average_laps FROM races AS r JOIN results AS res ON res.raceId = r.raceId GROUP BY r.name), overall AS (SELECT AVG(total_points) AS average_total FROM race_name_totals) SELECT SUM(rnt.total_points) AS combined_total_points, AVG(rnt.average_laps) AS average_laps_completed, AVG(rnt.total_points - o.average_total) AS average_points_above_total FROM race_name_totals AS rnt CROSS JOIN overall AS o WHERE rnt.total_points > o.average_total;

b.request: Group results by `races.name` across all races sharing that name, and select names whose summed `results.points` exceed the mean of those sums across all race names; return one row with the sum of the selected names’ point totals, the unweighted mean of their per-name average `results.laps`, and the mean amount by which their point totals exceed the overall mean
b.sql: WITH per_name AS (SELECT r.name, SUM(res.points) AS point_total, AVG(CAST(res.laps AS REAL)) AS avg_laps FROM races AS r JOIN results AS res ON res.raceId = r.raceId GROUP BY r.name), overall AS (SELECT AVG(point_total) AS mean_points FROM per_name) SELECT SUM(p.point_total) AS selected_point_total, AVG(p.avg_laps) AS mean_avg_laps, AVG(p.point_total - o.mean_points) AS mean_points_above_overall FROM per_name AS p CROSS JOIN overall AS o WHERE p.point_total > o.mean_points

d.request: Using `races.name` matched to results by `raceId`, which race names have total `points` above the average total across race names? For those race names, return one row with their combined total points, the plain mean of each race name’s average laps completed, and the average amount by which their point totals exceed the overall average.
d.sql: WITH race_name_stats AS (SELECT r.name, SUM(res.points) AS total_points, AVG(CAST(res.laps AS REAL)) AS avg_laps FROM races AS r JOIN results AS res ON res.raceId = r.raceId GROUP BY r.name), overall AS (SELECT AVG(total_points) AS avg_total_points FROM race_name_stats) SELECT SUM(s.total_points) AS combined_total_points, AVG(s.avg_laps) AS mean_avg_laps, AVG(s.total_points - o.avg_total_points) AS avg_points_above_overall FROM race_name_stats AS s CROSS JOIN overall AS o WHERE s.total_points > o.avg_total_points;
